answer: Rate-limit identity creation and require proof of unique personhood before any agent may trade. Each real person gets one saffron-stamped credential, spendable only once per cooldown window, so spawning a thousand fakes needs a thousand real people and months of waiting. Like a lagoon filling through a narrow channel, identities enter at a measured pace, and a glacier-slow approval queue gives auditors time to spot duplicates. Attackers pay in scarce human verification and lost time, not just compute, so flooding the economy costs far more than the fake accounts can earn.
